extracted.intended_audience: general literate public; aspiring essayists, conversationalists, gardeners, and members of fashionable society
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and evaluative criteria for writing (method vs irregularity), managing conversation and disputes, garden design aesthetics, and conduct/dress in polite society as given in Spectator essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical discourse (writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method is of advantage to a Work: have the whole scheme of the discourse in mind before setting pen to paper; place thoughts under proper heads so they follow one another in a regular series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits listed: helps invention (new thoughts arise from each head), makes thoughts more intelligible, better discovers drift and meaning, removes obscurity found in confusion, each thought shows its greatest beauty when properly placed, reader comprehends easily, takes in with pleasure, and retains long. Example contrast: methodical discourse like a regular plantation where one can view lines and walks; irregular like a wood where objects rise in confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregular/rambling style (when acceptable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregularity and want of method are only supportable in Men of great Learning or Genius, who are often too full to be exact, and therefore choose to throw down their Pearls in Heaps before the Reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use irregular, ‘rambling’ essay form (à la Seneca or Montaigne) only when authorial genius or extensive learning justifies it; such works allow the reader to 'ramble' and discover many new things but may leave only a confused, imperfect notion of the subject. The form is defensible for highly learned/authentic voices but not for ordinary writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Method is not less requisite in ordinary Conversation than in Writing, provided a Man would talk to make himself understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically: keep to the question at hand; avoid wandering from the point. An apparently learned disputant who cannot methodize thoughts will produce 'a barren Superfluity of Words'. Good conversationalists present thoughts in order so hearers comprehend; otherwise discussion becomes confused and meaningless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay on point; cut off irrelevancies in disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a disputant runs off the question, refocus him by asking 'What then? We allow all this to be true, but what is it to our present Purpose?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective disputation requires repeatedly asking what the speaker is trying to prove; refocusing stops long eloquence that fails to answer the original point. This is presented as a practical tactic (example: Will Dry silences Tom Puzzle by demanding the purpose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of a strong discussant
rubrics_metrics.description: A good disputant has a clear methodical head and few words; mere half-knowledge that raises doubts without clearing them leads to impertinence and contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast between 'Tom Puzzle' (enough reading to be impertinent but not enough to resolve doubts; habitually diverts to a few topics) and 'Will Dry' (concise, methodical, able to expose irrelevance). Guidance: prefer depth and method over flashy but unsubstantial learning; brevity combined with clarity wins debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden design: favour naturalistic (English) irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: English gardening should run into the beautiful Wildness of Nature, without affecting the nicer Elegancies of Art; mix kitchen, parterre, orchard and flower-garden so products of the same season appear together and compose a picture of variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rules: take in only plants that naturally rejoice in the soil; range products of same season together; value kitchen gardens for their wholesome luxury over artificial or foreign tender plants; create labyrinthine plantations where one cannot at a glance distinguish tree types; include fountains/rills that wander through plantings 'as it would do in an open Field' to enhance pleasure and plenty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden design: winter garden and bird-friendly practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Winter-Garden' of evergreens provides pleasure in bleak seasons; gardens should invite birds and not suffer destruction of nests or driving birds away in fruit-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winter-garden specifics: use ivy-covered walls, laurel, hornbeam, holly and other evergreen trees to create lively scenes in November/January; the red berries and verdure supply vernal delight in winter. Bird-friendly guidance: value blackbirds more than cherries; provide springs and shade, solitude and shelter; do not permit destruction of nests — preserve birds for seasonal music and as part of the garden's pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gardens as moral/aesthetic goods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pleasure taken in a Garden is one of the most innocent Delights in Human Life; it fills the mind with calmness and tranquility, lays turbulent Passions at rest, and suggests innumerable subjects for meditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing gardens as virtuous: taking complacent satisfaction in nature is a laudable habit of mind; gardens are associated with the habitation before the Fall and reveal Providence's contrivance and wisdom. This is presented as justification for cultivating pleasure in gardens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress and fashion as social tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothes make us agreeable objects; dress contributes to how people receive and express themselves — a bashful man may be raised to freedom by becoming well-dressed; a man of sense in negligent dress will be coldly received until proved otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical prescription: it is better to dress rather above one's fortune than under it; dress can hide imperfections and show beauties. The social function of dress includes influencing reception, maintaining ranks in society, and enabling duty/respect to attend appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion repository proposal (preservation and regulation of fashions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal for a Repository built for Fashions: a building with boxes like books, a Keeper knowledgeable in clothes, and divisions for each sex; inventors of fashions bring a box to record and preserve their designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons given: (1) help conceal or show personal defects in the most agreeable manner; (2) keep money in the kingdom by curbing travel for dress-finishings; (3) relieve scholars from wasting time describing ancient dress; (4) enable older people to vindicate their youth by showing fashions of past times. Implementation details: architectural imagery, motto, display features, and appointment of a Board of Directors and Keeper with fashion expertise.
